ETERNAL.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 conference-call transcript, opened and verified on 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects broadly flat food-delivery margins over the next one to two years while reinvesting in growth.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards. That's what the operating principle is. It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Store expansion will focus on smaller cities, where management reports favourable paybacks.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "That's right, Garima. Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on, and we are seeing great outcomes in terms of payback on these stores in these markets that we've expanded into in the last few quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Accelerating store additions from OND are not expected to reduce margins in the short term; management expects longer-term expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, it was a specific comment. What we are saying here is that as we accelerate store addition, which is starting OND, we don't expect that to hit the margins in the short term. Longer term, of course, margins will continue expanding, but we don't expect that there should be a short-term margin reduction on account of accelerated store addition."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts tested the faster store-expansion plan, smaller-city economics and paybacks.
Analysts asked whether competitive investment would cap food-delivery margins.

key_risks: Growth reinvestment is expected to keep food-delivery margins broadly flat for one to two years.
Blinkit margin expectations are forward-looking; faster additions may produce uneven store-throughput trends.

key_actuals.metric: Blinkit NOV per day per store
key_actuals.value: ₹9 lakh currently; management described about ₹11 lakh in steady state, with a potentially uneven path.

SHRIRAMFIN.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 conference-call transcript, opened and verified on 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 AUM growth expectation is 15%–17%, down from initial 18%, reflecting cautious growth amid weak monsoon and West Asia uncertainty.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Growth, we have been cautious, even though our initial guidance was 18% growth. Looking at the impact of the war situation in West Asia and the weak monsoon, we have been growing a little less than that. The first quarter, our growth was around 15%. In the second quarter, it was 17%. We will be anywhere growing anywhere between these two 15% to 17%. So we are very cautious in our growth."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

next_quarter_outlook.summary: NIM may remain elevated for one or two quarters, then move toward 9% medium term and 8.5% long term as capital is deployed.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "The net interest margin is because of th e capital infusion, there is a temporary increase in the NIM. It is likely to remain at this level maybe for another one quarter or two, then slowly coming down. So, in the medium term, it should come to around 9, then maybe in the long term, it will come to around 8.5."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management describes a temporary 30–40 bps credit-cost increase in some geographies, not a full-year increase; full-year cost could be below 2.3%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I said there will be temporary increase of 30 to 40 basis point, and not for the full year. So I feel the full year credit cost can be much lower than the 2.3. Temporarily, it may be for this quarter and next quarter."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Umesh Revankar

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts examined rising Stage 2/3 balances and provisioning.
Analysts questioned growth strategy amid lower borrower income and uncertainty.

bank_lender.credit_growth: AUM rose 16.96% YoY and 4.85% sequentially to INR3,29,021.72 crore. FY27 growth expectation is 15%–17%.
bank_lender.disbursements: Q2 disbursements grew 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crore.
bank_lender.nim_outlook: Q2 NIM 9.52%; expected to normalize toward 9% medium term and 8.5% long term.
bank_lender.credit_cost_outlook: Temporary 30–40 bps increase in some geographies; management explicitly says this is not full-year guidance.

key_risks: Weak monsoon and West Asia uncertainty drive caution on growth.
NIM uplift from capital infusion is temporary.
Temporary localized credit-cost pressure may persist into the next quarter.

In the second quarter, it was 17%. We will be anywhere growing anywhere between these two 15% to 17%. So we are very cautious in our growth."

INFY.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; verified exchange attachment.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 revenue growth guidance is 1%–2% in constant currency; operating margin guidance remains 20%–22%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Based on our Q2 performance and revised outlook fo r the rest of the year, our revenue growth guidance is 1% to 2% YoY in constant currency terms. Our operating margin guidance remains the same at 20% to 22%."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Salil Parekh

next_quarter_outlook.summary: H2 faces furloughs and fewer working days; guidance spans further uncertainty through environmental improvement.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, as you know, we are entering the seasonally weaker part of the year. There will be furloughs that will impact the H2, there will be lower working day s and all of those implications and all of those impacts. So that will definitely be there. And like always, we do not have one model that leads to guidance. There are always multiple models that leads to mult iple points of the guidance. At the lower end of the guidance, we have baked in higher uncertainty at the upper end of the guidance, we have baked in an improvement in the environment. At this point in time, we cannot really say where we will end up. I mean that is on how things play out."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts asked about risk to guidance and the effects of H2 seasonality.

key_risks: H2 furloughs and fewer working days constrain seasonal performance; uncertainty can affect the guidance outcome.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Lower bound -0.5 percentage point; upper bound -1 percentage point
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management describes the old range and revised range in the latest transcript.

evidence.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
evidence.quote: "So if you look at our guidance, our our last guidance was 1.5% to 3%. We had clearly called out at 1.5%, we expect even more uncertainty. Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain softer. We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity. So all that is baked in, in our revised guidance as we look forward. On top of that, as Salil said, some of the sectors, we see softness, Retail, Hi-Tech, where the discretionary is lower than what we are expecting. So all of that is reflected in our guidance on the revenue and which is where it is 1% to 2% now."

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects around INR3,500 crore recoveries in the coming quarter and INR12,000–13,000 crore for FY27, describing the upper outcome as challenging.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Yes. In fact, we were expecting in this quarter to have a recovery in the range of around INR 3,000 crores to INR 3,500 crores. But recovery always happens sometimes you initiate the process, but it slips to the next month or next quarter. So I am expecting at least in this quarter, the recovery should happen in the range of around INR 3,500 crores. So we will be trying to reach that figure around INR 13,000 crores figure. But of course, it is challenging figure, somewhere INR 12,000 crores to INR 13,000 crores will be there."

PGEL.description: NSE-filed Q1 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; latest qualifying transcript as of 29 October 2026.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management expects better commodity pass-through and aims for about 8% full-year operating margin, while explicitly calling this an aspiration rather than guidance.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "This year, on an overall basis, I'm expecting margins at the operating level, which is basically ex of PLI, ex of any incentive, etcetera, to improve significantly because that pass-through should be there. So on a reported basis, we should be having a slightly better margin than last year. And initially, at the beginning of this year, we had guided that we should be probably close to 8% kind of a margin for the whole year, at least at the operating level, which is this quarter about 7.3%. And we are hopefully going to reach that number on a full year basis."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Pramod Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Sri City refrigerator facility targets commercial production in Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenue from FY28.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Secondly, on our refrigerator facility at Sri City in South India, it is progressing well. We are targeting commercial production by quarter 4 of this financial year and with this becoming a meaningful revenue stream for FY '28 onwards. We have also tied up with our anchor customer for this business, and we are already active discussions with other customers also where we are getting some soft commitments from them."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vishal Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management sees 25%–30% growth potential in FY27 and FY28 as new capacity ramps, followed by possible consolidation in FY29.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So even if, say, '27, '28, I don't see any reason why we will not have 25%, 30% growth for us. And even if say for '29, if it is a consolidation year, we don't mind because in that year, we will be actually consolidating our position, getting our operations much more efficient and getting the profitability, which is ROCE, ROE, which is very important for us at a respectable level so that we can have money to invest in the next phase of growth. So that is what is going to be the strategy."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Pramod Gupta

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts tested when copper, aluminium and resin inflation would be recovered through customer pricing.
Questions focused on compressors, refrigerators, washing machines and the utilization of recent capex.

manufacturer.revenue_growth: Q1 consolidated revenue ₹2,034 crore, up 35.2% YoY.
manufacturer.volume_growth: Room AC volumes grew about 20%–22%; ASP increased about 10%–12%.
manufacturer.order_inflow: Not disclosed; management does not report firm order-book numbers.
manufacturer.demand_outlook: Management expects outsourcing share gains and 25%–30% company growth potential in FY27 and FY28.
manufacturer.margin_outlook: Commodity pass-through should improve; about 8% full-year operating margin is an aspiration, not formal guidance.
manufacturer.ebitda_margin: Q1 EBITDA margin 7.7%; operating margin excluding incentives about 7.3%.

key_risks: Commodity inflation and rupee depreciation may delay price pass-through and margin normalization.
Q4 refrigerator production and compressor ramp depend on project execution and customer uptake.
Management explicitly says the 8% margin figure is an aspiration, not guidance.

INDHOTEL.description: NSE-filed actual Q2 FY2027 earnings-call transcript; verified exchange attachment.

next_quarter_outlook.summary: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance increases to 15%–17%; Hotel segment revenue is expected to grow 17%–19%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Building on this strong foundation, sustained momentum and seasonally strong quarters ahead, we are confident of exceeding our previously communicated FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 12% to 14% by 300 basis points. Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%. And within that, the Hotel segment revenue is expected to grow by 17% to 19%."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Puneet Chhatwal

analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts examined whether the upgraded full-year guidance remained conservative entering a seasonally strong H2.

key_risks: Guidance accounts for slower TajSATS growth and a high Q4 comparison base.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Both bounds and midpoint increased 3 percentage points (300 basis points)
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management explicitly says it is revising full-year growth guidance upwards.

evidence.speaker: Puneet Chhatwal
evidence.role: Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
evidence.quote: "Building on this strong foundation, sustained momentum and seasonally strong quarters ahead, we are confident of exceeding our previously communicated FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 12% to 14% by 300 basis points. Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%. And within that, the Hotel segment revenue is expected to grow by 17% to 19%."

key_actuals.value: ₹706 crore, up 24% YoY; operating EBITDA margin 28.4%, up 50 basis points.
